title: 2D Contour: the first tabbed level moves the lead-in to a new point and plunges the full 18 mm in one feed move, half in uncut sheet; verify passes

body:
Found by the QA swarm round 2 (#2582), brief q07 (MDF bracket, 18 mm sheet), CamCraft **v0.25.0** Linux x86_64 release, Sienci AltMill 4x4, post grblHAL. The G-code was read by hand.

## What happens

ProfileCutout: 2D Contour, side outside, picked outer chain, entry plunge, stepdown 4.5, 4 tabs (width 10, height 3), bottom = bottom of model - 0.3, Router up-cut 6 mm. The untabbed levels (Z -4.5, -9, -13.5, -15.3) all lead in at the same point (X258.066 Y2.09), so each plunge is one stepdown into the kerf of the level above. The first tabbed level moves the lead-in to the inside corner of the L and plunges from Z2 straight to the final depth:

```
G0 X242.068 Y1.89 Z25
G0 X246.667 Y90.812 Z25
G0 X246.667 Y90.812 Z2
G1 X246.667 Y90.812 Z-18 F600
G1 X253.739 Y87.072 Z-18 F1950
```

The upper levels cut along Y 88 there (kerf Y 85..91), so the Ø6 cutter centred at Y 90.812 (Y 87.8..93.8) plunges 18 mm with a 2.8 mm crescent of never-cut sheet beside it, at the plunge feed. Each tab hop then also feeds from Z -18 up to Z 12 and plunges 30 mm back down at F600 (lines 464-470 and on). The same happens on the Z -18.3 level. `verify` reports `ok: true`, no findings.

## Expected

Each level enters at most one stepdown below the floor the levels above left at the entry point (the same lead-in point as the untabbed levels, or a ramp), and tab hops rise only to the tab top plus a clearance.

## Repro files

[q07-router.camproj](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.camproj), [q07-router.step](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.step), posted [q07-router.nc](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.nc) (operation ProfileCutout from line 372; the tabbed level at lines 456-490); agent report [REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/REPORT.md) problem 8.

How bad: no gouge of the part; a full-length plunge into partly uncut stock that the program's own stepdown says never happens, a cutter-breakage risk on small router bits.

Done means: on this project every ProfileCutout level enters no deeper than one stepdown below the cut floor at its entry point (pinned by a test with tabs on a multi-level contour), and verify or the op notes name a plunge deeper than the stepdown into uncut stock.
